t: Sum of Mutated Array Closest to Target — Binary Search on the Answer
o: We pick a value `value`; every element of `arr` greater than it is replaced by it, and we want the resulting sum as close to `target` as possible (ties broken by smaller value). The mutated sum is a non-decreasing, piecewise-linear function of `value`, so we can search over candidate values. In example 1 (`[4,9,3]`, target 10), choosing 3 gives [3,3,3] = 9; choosing 4 gives 12, so 3 wins. In example 2, value 5 leaves the array unchanged with sum exactly 10. Constraints ($n \le 10^4$, values $\le 10^5$) make even an $O(n \cdot V)$ scan feasible, but binary search gives a clean $O(n \log V)$ solution.
k: The mutated sum is monotonically non-decreasing in `value`, which enables binary search on the answer.
The optimal `value` lies between 0 and max(arr); above max(arr) the sum stops changing.
On ties in absolute difference, prefer the smaller value — check this explicitly after binary search.

a.n: Approach 1: Brute Force over Candidate Values
a.i: Try every integer value from 0 to max(arr), compute the mutated sum for each, and keep the best. Correct because the answer must lie in that range and each check is straightforward. Simple but slow: $O(n \cdot V)$ where $V$ can be $10^5$.
s: Let hi = max(arr). For value from 0 to hi:
Compute sum by capping each element at value (use prefix sums + sorting to do this fast per candidate if desired).
Track the value minimizing |sum - target|, preferring smaller value on ties.
a.t: O(n log n + n·V) — sorting plus one capped-sum evaluation per candidate value (V up to 10^5).

a.n: Approach 2: Binary Search on the Answer (Optimal)
a.i: Since the mutated sum only grows as `value` increases, binary search the smallest `value` whose mutated sum is >= target. That value and value-1 are the only candidates for the optimum; pick whichever has smaller absolute difference, preferring the smaller on ties. This avoids scanning all values.
s: Sort arr and build prefix sums so any mutated sum is computed in O(log n).
Binary search value in [0, max(arr)] for the smallest value with mutatedSum(value) >= target.
Return value-1 on tie or if it's strictly better; otherwise return value.
a.t: O(n log n + log V · log n) — sorting, then ~log V binary search steps each doing an O(log n) sum lookup.

w: In an interview, go straight to binary search on the answer after noting the monotonicity of the mutated sum; mention brute force briefly as motivation. Key pitfalls: forgetting the tie rule (return the smaller value, hence comparing `lo - 1` with `<=`), searching only up to max(arr) (values above it change nothing), and integer overflow when computing n * value in Java/C++ (use long). Edge cases: single-element arrays, target larger than total sum (answer = max(arr)), and target very small (answer near 0). Follow-ups may ask for an O(n log n)-only solution without nested binary search (solve via sorting + linear scan of breakpoints), or how to handle floating-point targets.
